title: Context as an Environment: Programmatic Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents

visual_explainer.question: What changes when long context becomes a lossless queryable environment instead of serialized prompt text?
visual_explainer.takeaway: An append-only event log and persistent Python namespace let the agent materialize only question-relevant state at query time while keeping the full history recoverable.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same QwenPaw harness without the persistent REPL, without its eviction index, and with lossy ingestion summaries.

analysis.tldr: Scroll treats long context as a lossless event log plus persistent Python environment and lets the model decide what to materialize into the prompt. The matched BEAM10M ablation supports the programmatic state interface; cross-system SOTA comparisons and complete lifecycle costs do not.
analysis.problem: Serializing all history into a prompt wastes attention, while lossy summaries and fixed retrieval can discard state whose future value is not yet known.
analysis.core_idea: Append events without LLM ingestion, preserve a Python namespace across turns, and let the agent issue programmatic queries/aggregation over an eviction index before printing only selected evidence back into context.
analysis.agent_loop: append event → retain queryable state → formulate Python query → aggregate/filter history → print selected evidence → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: History remains lossless outside the prompt; retrieval and computation are deferred until the information need is known. The REPL and index are separable through within-harness ablations.
compared_to: same Scroll harness without persistent REPL
CodeAct on LOCA under the same model
analysis.evidence: On BEAM10M, full scores 73.1 versus 65.8 without persistent REPL, 71.3 without the index, and 19.9 with lossy ingestion. On LOCA, Scroll ties CodeAct at 128K and leads by only 1.4 points at 256K.
analysis.why_it_matters: It makes context materialization an agent operation and separates retained recoverable state from what the model reads on a given step.
limitations: Most LOCA robustness comes from programmatic tool/state binding; Scroll's unique increment over CodeAct is small.
Published memory-system comparisons are unmatched on backbone, reader, retrieval budget, and judge.
Scroll trails some systems on summarization, temporal reasoning, and preference following.
Weaker backbones collapse on LOCA-256K, exposing dependence on program synthesis ability.
No matched latency, dollar, storage/index CPU, or lifecycle-update accounting is reported.
